chapter: Massey Hall, race and the record business
title: Poor whites enslaved by the same people
summary: Mingus reconsiders blanket anti-white feeling and talks about strikers, miners and Ford.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: did. And anybody who thinks that isn't true, it's surprising how many are lurking, with titles, and they're a part of the government. It's very sad. Do you really think that --

See, I really -- I made one mistake in my life, I'm talking about racial prejudice. I always say the white people, well, the white people were enslaved by the same -- the poor white people, the working class, are enslaved by the same people that enslaved the black people.
Like, these pickets, of the coal miners, the farmers. They'll start shooting at them the same way they do black people.
They have shot at them in the past.
And during the '20s and '30s, strikers at Ford Motor Car Company and other places like that were brutally beaten and shot to death and arrested and never heard of again.
Well, Ford was with the Nazis, wasn't he?
I read it someplace. There was a program on television, not long ago.
I hadn't heard that, but nothing would surprise me, frankly.
